title: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
blurb: Sixty-three years in Makkah and Madinah. The Quran is revealed, a community is built, and Arabia is united.

events.title: Birth of the Prophet ﷺ
events.what: Muhammad ﷺ is born in Makkah to Aminah, his father Abdullah having died before his birth.

events.title: Halimah and the opening of the chest

place.name: Lands of Banu Sa'd, near Taif

events.what: Raised in the desert by his nurse Halimah, the young boy is visited by Jibril, who opens his chest and washes his heart.
events.note: Reported by Muslim from Anas. Some link 94:1 to this event; most commentators read it as the opening of his heart to guidance.

events.title: An orphan at six
events.what: Returning from Madinah, his mother Aminah dies at al-Abwa. His grandfather Abd al-Muttalib takes him in, and two years later his uncle Abu Talib.

events.title: The monk Bahira
events.what: On a trading trip to Syria with Abu Talib, the boy is noticed by the monk Bahira, who sees in him the signs of a prophet and warns his uncle to guard him.
events.note: Reported by al-Tirmidhi and in the seerah. Scholars accept the core of the story but question some details of the report.

events.title: The Sacrilegious War
events.what: Quraysh and Hawazin fight the Fijar war, breaking the truce of the sacred months. The young Muhammad ﷺ gathers arrows for his uncles.
events.note: Ibn Ishaq gives his age as fourteen or twenty; the dates of the war vary.

events.title: Gregory the Great
events.what: Gregory the Great becomes Pope in Rome and sends monks to convert the English. The Western church gathers around the papacy.
events.tie: Within a generation the Quran would address these churches as People of the Book, calling them to a common word (3:64).

events.title: The Pact of the Virtuous
events.what: After a visiting merchant is cheated, clans of Makkah swear in the house of Abdullah ibn Jud'an to stand with anyone wronged. He takes part and never forgets it.
events.note: His later words, that he would answer such a call even in Islam, are reported by Ibn Ishaq and al-Bayhaqi.

events.title: Marriage to Khadijah
events.what: Known in Makkah as al-Amin, the trustworthy, he marries the merchant Khadijah. She is 40, he is 25.

events.title: The last war of the old empires
events.what: The emperor Maurice is murdered and Khosrow II of Persia invades Byzantium. A war of 26 years drains both empires of men and money.
events.tie: Surah ar-Rum was revealed in the middle of this war, and both worn-out empires lost their eastern lands to the Muslims soon after it.

events.title: The Black Stone
events.what: Quraysh rebuild the Kaaba and quarrel over who sets the Black Stone. He places it on a cloth so every clan can lift it.

events.title: Harsha's India
events.what: King Harsha rules northern India from Kannauj. The Chinese monk Xuanzang studies at his court and at the great Buddhist university of Nalanda.
events.tie: Arab merchants already sailed to India's coasts, and Islam reached Sindh by land and sea within a century (711).
events.note: A mosque at Kodungallur in Kerala is traditionally dated to the Prophet's lifetime, but there is no firm evidence for the date.

events.title: The first revelation
events.what: In the cave of Hira, Jibril brings the first words of the Quran: Read. Revelation begins on Laylat al-Qadr.

events.title: Waraqa's word
events.what: Shaking, he comes home from Hira. Khadijah comforts him and takes him to her cousin Waraqa, an old Christian scholar, who says this is the angel that came to Musa.

events.title: Arise and warn
events.what: After a pause in revelation, he sees Jibril again between sky and earth. Surah al-Muddaththir comes down: Arise and warn. The mission begins.
events.note: Reports differ on how long the pause in revelation lasted.

events.title: The call from Safa
events.what: After three years of quiet preaching, he calls Quraysh openly from Mount Safa. Abu Lahab curses him. Persecution begins.

events.title: Rome is defeated
events.what: Persia takes Jerusalem from Byzantium. The Quran predicts Rome will win again within a few years.
events.tie: Makkah's idol-worshippers cheered Persia's win while the Muslims sided with Christian Rome; Surah ar-Rum answered that Rome would win again within a few years (30:2-4).

events.title: Bilal: One, One
events.what: His master Umayyah lays a rock on Bilal's chest in the desert sun. Bilal answers only: One, One. Abu Bakr buys him and sets him free.
events.note: Many commentators say 92:17-21 speak of Abu Bakr, who spent his wealth freeing tortured slaves.

events.title: Refuge in Abyssinia
events.what: Persecuted Muslims flee to Christian Abyssinia. The Najashi hears Surah Maryam recited and refuses to hand them over.

events.title: Sumayyah, the first martyr
events.what: Sumayyah, a woman with no tribe to protect her, refuses to give up Islam and is killed by Abu Jahl. She is the first martyr of Islam.
events.note: Commentators say 16:106 was revealed about her son Ammar, forced under torture to say words of disbelief. 'Patience, family of Yasir, your promised place is Paradise' is reported by al-Hakim and al-Tabarani.

events.title: Pakal of Palenque
events.what: Pakal the Great rules the Maya city of Palenque for 68 years and is buried in a carved tomb, while to the north great Teotihuacan lies in ruins.
events.tie: The Quran says no nation was left without a warner (35:24), even peoples whose stories it does not tell (40:78).

events.title: Hamzah and Umar
events.what: Hamzah, the Prophet's uncle, and then Umar, once a fierce enemy, accept Islam. Muslims pray openly at the Kaaba.

events.title: The boycott
events.what: Quraysh boycott his clan for three years. No trade, no marriage. Children cry from hunger in the valley.

events.title: The Tang dynasty
events.what: The Tang dynasty begins in China. Its capital Chang'an is the largest city on earth. Muslim traders arrive by sea and land.
events.tie: In 651 envoys of the caliph Uthman reached the Tang court, the first official contact between China and the Muslims, recorded in Chinese annals.

events.title: The Year of Sorrow
events.what: Khadijah and Abu Talib die. He goes to Taif for help and is stoned out of the city. The Year of Sorrow.

events.title: The day at Taif
events.what: Taif's leaders set boys to stone him out of town. The angel of the mountains offers to crush those who rejected him. He refuses, hoping their children will worship Allah.
events.note: Ibn Ishaq adds that Addas, a Christian servant from Nineveh, brought him grapes and believed when he spoke of Yunus as his brother prophet.

events.title: The jinn listen
events.what: At Nakhlah, as he recites the Quran in prayer, a band of jinn stop to listen. They believe and go back to their people as warners.
events.note: Ibn Ishaq places this on the way back from Taif. A report from Ibn Abbas in al-Bukhari and Muslim places a listening at Nakhlah during the dawn prayer. Scholars say the jinn came more than once.

events.title: The Night Journey
events.what: The night journey from Makkah to Jerusalem, then up through the heavens. The five daily prayers are given.

events.title: The pledges of Aqabah
events.what: Men from Yathrib pledge loyalty at Aqabah. A second, larger pledge follows in 622. Madinah opens its doors.

events.title: The Hijrah
events.what: Quraysh plot to kill him. He and Abu Bakr hide in the cave of Thawr, then reach Madinah. The Islamic calendar starts here.

events.title: A new community
events.what: The Prophet's mosque is built. Each migrant is paired with a local brother, and a written charter binds Madinah's tribes.

events.title: The Charter of Madinah
events.what: A written charter makes the Muslims, the Jewish clans and the Arab tribes of Madinah one community for defence. Disputes go to Allah and His Messenger.
events.note: The text survives through Ibn Ishaq and Abu Ubayd. Historians debate whether it was one document or several agreements made over time.

events.title: The qiblah changes
events.what: The direction of prayer changes from Jerusalem to the Kaaba. Fasting in Ramadan is made obligatory the same year.

events.title: The Battle of Badr
events.what: 313 Muslims face 1,000 Quraysh at Badr. Angels fight with them. Abu Jahl is killed. The Quran calls it the Day of Criterion.

events.title: Banu Qaynuqa
events.what: Weeks after Badr, a quarrel in the market of the Banu Qaynuqa turns deadly and the tribe breaks its pact. After a siege they leave Madinah for Syria.
events.note: Ibn Ishaq reports that 3:12-13 were said to them in their market after Badr. Abdullah ibn Ubayy pleaded for them.

events.title: The Battle of Uhud
events.what: Archers leave their post and Quraysh strike back. Hamzah is killed, the Prophet ﷺ wounded. A lesson in obedience.

events.title: The well of Ma'unah
events.what: Seventy reciters of the Quran, sent to teach in Najd, are ambushed and killed at the well of Ma'unah. For a month he prays against the killers.
events.note: Reported by al-Bukhari from Anas. The same season another small group of teachers was betrayed at al-Raji'. The well's exact site is uncertain.

events.title: The Banu Nadir
events.what: The Banu Nadir plot to drop a stone on him from a roof. Besieged in their forts, they leave for Khaybar, pulling down their own houses. Surah al-Hashr tells it.
events.note: Ibn Abbas called al-Hashr 'the surah of Banu Nadir' (reported by al-Bukhari).

events.title: Dhat al-Riqa'
events.what: On a hard march into Najd, the men wrap their torn feet in rags. Facing an enemy, they pray the prayer of fear in turns, weapons in hand.
events.note: Ibn Ishaq dates it to 4 AH; al-Bukhari places it after Khaybar (7 AH) because Abu Musa, who explains the name 'the one with the rags', took part.

events.title: The Trench
events.what: Ten thousand allied tribes besiege Madinah. On Salman's advice the Muslims dig a trench. A wind breaks the siege.

events.title: Banu al-Mustaliq
events.what: On campaign, Abdullah ibn Ubayy says the honoured will drive the humble out of Madinah. Young Zayd ibn Arqam reports it, and Surah al-Munafiqun confirms him.
events.note: Dated to 5 AH by Musa ibn Uqbah and Ibn Sa'd, to 6 AH by Ibn Ishaq. His marriage to Juwayriyah, the chief's daughter, led the Companions to free her captive people.

events.title: The slander against Aisha
events.what: Left behind on the march home, Aisha is brought back by a Companion, and hypocrites spread a lie. After a month of pain, verses of Surah an-Nur declare her innocent.

events.title: Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
events.what: A ten-year truce with Quraysh that looks like a loss. The Quran calls it a clear victory. Islam spreads fast in the peace.

events.title: Letters to the kings
events.what: He sends letters inviting Heraclius of Byzantium, Khosrow of Persia, the Najashi and the ruler of Egypt to Islam.

events.title: Khaybar
events.what: The fortified Jewish oasis of Khaybar, which backed the siege of Madinah, surrenders after Ali takes its strongest fort.

events.title: Rome wins again
events.what: Heraclius crushes Persia at Nineveh. Surah ar-Rum's prediction comes true within the stated few years.
events.tie: Abu Bakr had wagered with Quraysh, before betting was forbidden, that Rome would win; the Quran had said 'that day the believers will rejoice' (30:4).

events.title: The pledge under the tree
events.what: A rumour says Uthman, sent as envoy to Makkah, has been killed. Under a tree some 1,400 Companions pledge to stand firm. Allah says He is pleased with them.
events.note: The number is given as 1,400 or 1,500 in al-Bukhari and Muslim.

events.title: The Battle of Mu'tah
events.what: 3,000 Muslims meet a far larger Byzantine army. Three commanders fall in turn. Khalid brings the army home.

events.title: Heraclius questions Abu Sufyan
events.what: Heraclius, in Jerusalem after his victory, questions Abu Sufyan about the Prophet ﷺ. Each answer convinces him, but his court rages and he keeps his throne.
events.tie: Abu Sufyan, still an enemy, could not lie before his own men, so a Roman emperor heard the truth about Islam from its opponent.

events.title: The fulfilled umrah
events.what: As agreed at Hudaybiyyah, the Muslims return for three days of umrah while Quraysh watch from the hills. The vision of 48:27 comes true.
events.note: The Companions jogged the first rounds to show Quraysh their strength (al-Bukhari, from Ibn Abbas). On this visit he married Maymunah.

events.title: The return to Makkah
events.what: Quraysh break the truce. Ten thousand Muslims enter Makkah without a battle. The idols are cleared from the Kaaba. All are pardoned.

events.title: The Battle of Hunayn
events.what: The tribes of Hawazin ambush the army in a valley. Early panic, then victory. The Quran warns against pride in numbers.

events.title: The march to Tabuk
events.what: A long march north to meet a rumoured Byzantine army. No battle, but the hypocrites who stayed home are exposed.

events.title: Prayer for the Najashi
events.what: The Najashi of Abyssinia, who sheltered the first Muslim refugees, dies. The Prophet ﷺ tells the people the same day and leads his funeral prayer in Madinah.
events.note: Reported by al-Bukhari and Muslim. Scholars hold the Najashi had accepted Islam.

events.title: The Year of Delegations
events.what: Tribes from across Arabia send delegations to accept Islam. The Year of Delegations.

events.title: The Hajj of Abu Bakr
events.what: Abu Bakr leads the Hajj. Ali reads the opening of Surah at-Tawbah: after this year no idolater may make Hajj, and none may circle the Kaaba naked.

quote.from: And [due] to Allah from the people is a pilgrimage

events.note: Scholars differ on when Hajj became obligatory: 6, 9 or 10 AH. The proclamation is reported by al-Bukhari from Abu Hurayrah.

events.title: The Farewell Hajj
events.what: He leads the Hajj with over 100,000 pilgrims and gives his farewell sermon. The verse completing the religion is revealed.

events.title: The Prophet ﷺ passes away
events.what: He dies in Aisha's room in Madinah. Abu Bakr steadies the shocked community: Muhammad has died, but Allah lives.

events.title: Ibrahim and the eclipse
events.what: His baby son Ibrahim dies and the sun goes dark. People say it is for Ibrahim. He tells them the sun and moon do not eclipse for anyone's death.
events.note: An annular eclipse crossed Arabia on 27 January 632, matching the reports. Weeping, he said: the eye sheds tears and the heart grieves, but we say only what pleases our Lord.

events.title: The last verses
events.what: Shortly before his death the final verses come down. Many scholars say the very last was: And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah.
events.note: 5:3, revealed at Arafat, completes the religion but is not the last verse by most accounts. Ibn Abbas named 2:281 (al-Nasa'i) and the verses on usury (al-Bukhari); al-Bara named 4:176 (al-Bukhari).
